chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two of them, peace be upon them, about the deceased, and he said: “He is to be drawn out from the direction of the feet, and the grave is to be made level with the ground except to the measure of four spread fingers, and his grave is to be made four-sided.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ: the measure of four fingers, indicating the grave’s slight elevation
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person being discussed in the burial ruling
key_terms.مُفَرَّجَاتٍ: spread apart, describing the width measure of the fingers
key_terms.يُرَبَّعُ: is made four-sided or squared in form
key_terms.يُسَلُّ: is drawn out or extracted, here referring to moving the deceased from the side of the feet

ai.seo_question: How should the grave of a deceased person be prepared according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the burial of the deceased. It describes how the body is to be removed, how high the grave should be raised above the ground, and that the grave should be shaped in a four-sided manner.
